The solution is the line concept with these lines, vehicles and total travel time. In the second iteration we solve MCCLPP where lines from the first iteration are extended by lines created from OD pair (s, t) so that the shortest s-t path does not lie on any chosen lines. In the (k+1)-th iteration we solve MCCLPP from chosen links of k-th iteration and extended links as in the second iteration. Algorithm ends if two consequent iterations have same line concept. This approach is demonstrated via illustrative example.

articleTitle: Velocity information reconstruction in an energy harvesting magnetorheological damper
abstract: The work summarises experimental tests of velocity sensing capability in an energy harvesting MR damper (EHMRD). Data obtained from displacement, velocity and acceleration sensors under the idle run of the device were duly analysed, processed and discussed. The relationship was established between electromotive force (emf) and velocity across the EHMRD. The results highlight the potential application of the EHMRD as a velocity sensor, exploring its suitability for use in smart vibration control systems.

articleTitle: The movable mechatronic kinetic sculpture with glass pendants on electronic cams
abstract: This article deals with the movable mechatronic kinetic sculpture with glass pendants on electronic cams. The aim of the work is to transform the initial idea of the designer's shapes and movements of the sculpture simulation to the final realization. The main topic of the article is the displacement law, in other words the electronic cams. Specifically the solution of the calculation of individual displacement law by the 5th degree polynomial with the possibility of a correction in the graphical environment in the design time and in the time of finishing the final form. Electronic, mechanical and programming equipment was developed. The smooth, quiet and dynamic movement of the independent metal-glass elements, synchronized with the lighting. Compared to the standard single-purpose tasks of the automated manufacturing machine type, the project's goal is an artistic impression. The result is a movable mechatronic kinetic sculpture with twenty servomotors and six scenes, controlled by the PLC, iPad interface and complete remote management because of the location Guangzhou, southern China. Although the resulting project is unique, it allows similar or innovative solutions in other realizations that come from the designers of moving kinetic sculptures.

articleTitle: Reproducing the magnetic hysteretic behaviour of an MR squeeze-mode actuator
abstract: In the study the authors reproduce the magnetic hysteretic behaviour of an MR squeeze mode (MRSQ) actuator by investigating its current-flux relationship. For this purpose voltage and current measurements were performed. This is demonstrated using a sensorless magnetic flux estimation technique. The authors reveal the response of the actuator when subjected to sinusoidal inputs across a wide range of operating conditions and excitation inputs. The observation of the flux data shows that the hysteresis is influenced by both amplitude and the frequency of the excitation input as well as piston position.

articleTitle: Novel approach to robust PI controller design with state derivative feedback for linear uncertain systems
abstract: The paper devoted is to the problem of develop robust PI controller design procedure for uncertain linear systems with state derivative feedback. The obtained continuous-time PI robust controller with output/state and state derivative feedback ensure the guaranteed cost and parameter dependent quadratic stability in frame of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The novel results are that the designed robust PI controller is used for stabilization of closed loop systems with the state derivative feedback. Due to new auxiliary matrices the design procedure gives less conservativeness results. Numerical example is given to illustrate the properties and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Responsive graphical user interface (ReGUI) and its implementation in MATLAB
abstract: In this paper the responsive graphical user interface (ReGUI) approach to creating applications is introduced, and the requirements to the ReGUI applications are defined. Implementation of the ReGUI approach is outlined and illustrated on a sample application developed in MATLAB for supporting teaching of extrema of the functions of two variables. The same general technique can be used in other programming languages. The code and the demonstration video are available through the MATLAB Central File Exchange.

articleTitle: Visualisation of mathematical content using LATEX animations
abstract: Animations have become most valuable contents in mathematical education. There are many tools for creating animations. This article presents creating animations using the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sup>T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub>X Animate package. This package creates JavaScript driven PDF animations from a set of image files, inline graphics or typeset text. In this article we demonstrate animations of solving mathematical examples from set of image files and animations using inline PGF/TikZ generated pictures. PGF and TikZ are packages for creating graphics integrated with L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sup>T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub>X and Beamer.

articleTitle: Model-based control system design for steam turbine based on Functional Mock-up interface (FMI/FMU)
abstract: This paper exploits the authors recent work where real-time simulator of the steam turbine was developed using mathematical-physical modeling. Consequently, this work focuses on exact feedback controller design. Firstly, the steam turbine model was linearized for operations in the so-called island and national grid mode. Further, the generalized robustness regions method was applied to design 2DOF PI/PID controller for both working modes. Fulfilling design requirements (sensitivity function limits, gain and phase margins) ensures the required robustness of feedback loop. Using export to FMU (Functional Mock-up Unit), the resulted controller was validated in real-time in both SiL (Software-in-the-Loop) and HiL (Hardware-in-the-Loop) schemes. The presented procedure allows rapid optimization/re-tuning/adaptation of controller in case the model is changed. It is supposed that similar procedure will be applied on other energetic devices (water turbine, power generator, drum boiler, etc.).

articleTitle: Development of an HMI using JAVA for monitoring and control of automated systems applied in distributed control systems
abstract: Nowadays in the industry, machines are responsible for controlling and triggering many processes, which contrasts with the fact that monitoring a large number of operations is an arduous task for a single human. However, the DCSs were created to allow only a human to be able to monitor and act on various processes through a central device equipped with an HMI. This paper discusses the development of an HMI dedicated to a DCS. The system has a control and data acquisition unit composed by an Arduino MEGA 2560 and an Ethernet Module. There is also an Ethernet communication network and an HMI developed in JAVA language. It is known that communication networks are critical parts of a DCS, as well as the possible delays that may exist. Therefore, this work brings a study and application on Ethernet networks and means to obtain better performance in sending and receiving data. The developed HMI operates with two transport protocols: TCP and UDP. In this way, it was possible to perform a comparison between the performance of both protocols, being useful for classroom activities, such as in undergraduate courses.

articleTitle: Practical method for designing robust RBF-MRAC neurocontrollers: The first-order case
abstract: The model reference adaptive control (MRAC) system built with radial basis function (RBF) neural network proved to be useful in controlling nonlinear plants. In this paper a novel method is proposed for designing RBF-MRAC neurocontrollers. The resulted RBF network is optimal in minimal norm-product sense, and the method can be used in case of plants' known nonlinear function. The robustness of the resulted controller was investigated with simulations concerning both parameter tolerances of the nonlinearity and abrupt disturbances. In case of unknown nonlinearity a heuristic method is given, which also resulted in a robust solution. The simulation results of the neurocontroller are also presented in the paper in case of several nonlinearities.

articleTitle: State control design for discrete-time systems with state constraints
abstract: The paper examines the problem of state feedback control design, building on the dissipative principle and the slack matrix approach. Prescribing the system inputs to be less than or equal to defined bounds, the existence of feedback control law parameters is given in terms of the solvability of a set of linear matrix inequalities, ensuring in addition that the state variables will be constrained in ellipsoidal positive invariant set. Presented numerical examples illustrate practical validity and efficiency of the methodology.

articleTitle: Rotational speed estimation using the discrete Kalman filtering applied to a tacho signal
abstract: The paper deals with Kalman's filtering for the rotational speed time history of rotors, which is determined by the use of a tacho-signal that is composed of the string of pulses each of them is generated at least once per the complete rotor revolution. The accuracy of the estimation of the time interval length corresponding to the one complete revolution depends on the number of samples which corresponds to the mentioned time interval. The reciprocal value of the length of this interval determines the rotation frequency. If the rotation speed is multiply increased, the measurement error increases considerably as well. The Kalman filter is a suitable means for smoothing the rotational speed measurement by reducing the measurement error.

articleTitle: Design of observer-based state feedback control
abstract: One step technique for observer-based control design of the discrete-time linear systems with unknown disturbance is presented. It enables to formulate design conditions as the set of linear matrix inequalities constructing the enhanced bounded real lemma structure and stating that the controller-observer parameter separation in design is not strictly required in this case. Since the input, output and disturbance, jointly constrained by the equations of the system, are taking into account, better results considering the closed-loop system performances can be obtained, since they are jointly constrained by the equations of the observed system The example is presented to demonstrate the design advantages of the embraced methodology.

articleTitle: Optimization of control parameters of production refractory materials in tunnel furnace
abstract: The paper deals with the optimal adjustment of process control parameters for burning of refractory materials in a tunnel furnace. So-called optimization system with model was used for setting optimal parameters, which includes an optimization algorithm for finding optimal parameters. The paper presents a gradient method application in the said system for determining optimal parameters. Qualitative criteria of material heating are the optimality criterion, which minimizes the temperature difference between the model and the required batch temperature.

articleTitle: Situational awareness in HMI of industrial plants
abstract: In this article, implementation of Situational Awareness in complex control systems is discussed. Motivation factors and the process of Situational Awareness achievement are described. Human Machine Interface (HMI) design methodology of such a system is laid out. Library of Situational Awareness HMI (SA HMI) components is presented. Layout of higher level HMI providing projection of real time process information into the production plant major business goal is presented.

articleTitle: An introduction to class of fractional-order extremal control: First results
abstract: This paper introduces a class of fractional-order extremal control that is based on sign changes of the derivative of the controlled value. For the first time, the control loop consists of a controlled process of the Wiener type described by a fractional-order linear model, and a term with extremal characteristic (parabolic nonlinearity). An illustrative example presents results obtained for the temperature control of an electrical heater.

articleTitle: Security system based on microcontrollers
abstract: The article describes design and realization of security system based on single-chip microcontrollers. System includes sensor modules for unauthorized entrance detection based on magnetic contact, measuring carbon monoxide level, movement detection and measuring temperature and humidity. System also includes control unit, control panel and development board Arduino with ethernet interface connected for web server implementation.

articleTitle: CompactRIO control system for active vibration control
abstract: This paper deals with the use of CompactRIO control system developed by National Instruments as a control system for active vibration control of a test device. For the control, it was necessary to ensure a high-speed sampling rate, which was ensured by the field programmable gate array (FPGA). The CompactRIO control system is programmed using the LabVIEW software tool.

articleTitle: Challenges of I4.0 smart control processes in electronics manufacturing
abstract: Jabil is an EMS company providing electronics manufacturing services for our clients. The company was established in 1966. Jabil has 90 facilities in 23 countries, and 175,000 employees worldwide. Jabil uses latest manufacturing technologies because the industry is moving very fast. We experience shorter and shorter periods for new product introduction and the time between two following generations is continuously reduced. Same time the components are shrinking, the integration of the circuits is higher and the density of components goes to extreme in some sectors like mobile devices. Thus, Jabil works on Industry 4.0 solutions in the last few years to serve better the customer demands.

articleTitle: Embedded control system for an aircraft two-spool jet engine with coolant injection into the compressor
abstract: The paper deals with an aircraft two-spool single-jet engine's control system; basic control system (based on a fuel flow controller and an exhaust nozzle controller) is completed by a new controller (of the injected coolant flow rate). The paper has studied possible engine control architecture and established its mathematical model. Considering the engine as controlled object and its thrust the most important operation effect, one has chosen as main outputs spools' rotational speeds, as secondary output the combustor's temperature, while as single input - engine's power lever displacement. Based on embedded system's main parts' mathematical models, the author has described the embedded control system by its block diagram with transfer functions; furthermore, some Simulink-Matlab simulations are performed, concerning embedded system quality (its output parameters time behavior) and, meanwhile, some conclusions concerning engine's parameters mutual influences are revealed.

articleTitle: On the use of evolutionary algorithms in estimation of permittivity
abstract: Evolutionary algorithms used in non-explicit inverse problems may represent a crucial helpful instrument. This work deals with estimation of complex permittivity. Current work widens previous theoretical knowledge and emphasizes on the progress in this field. Backward reconstruction of complex permittivity of single and multi-layered structures in free space in the range of millimetre and sub-millimetre waves remains a challenging and up to date complex problem. The basis of proposed system is represented by a verified direct mathematical model (deduced from Maxwell's equations) computing scattering parameters of defined non-magnetic materials in free space (of known thicknesses and complex permittivities). Turning this explicit model over and thus using transmission coefficients as the input of the system and applying evolutionary algorithm on it (Particle Swarm Optimization has been chosen for this purpose in this case) provides a tool producing useful relatively precise and fast estimations of complex material permittivity.

articleTitle: Intelligent and suitable transportation system with asynchronous motor and Li-Ion battery
abstract: In the case of modern transport systems, the dualism drive system - power supply is represented by the power converter unit and asynchronous electric motor - Li-Ion battery. These asynchronous motors taken separately cannot answer to dynamic requirements, their command at the control loop level being generally complex, and moreover the converters have embedded sophisticated control systems. In order to solve all these problems, a detailed investigation was necessary to allow proper evaluation of both the main dynamic parameters of transportation system and a proper modeling of Li-Ion battery system. The paper deals with an analysis of the electric transportation systems, with details concerning the management of electric system. Some important problems such as the energy integrated control of the vehicle, innovative solutions for converters adapted to the typical electric vehicle voltage levels and reduction of the harmonics content in the PWM control are approached.

articleTitle: Determination of factors modifying land value based on spatial data
abstract: Land market is special because its overall offer is relatively fixed by its nature. Moreover, it primarily acts upon local supply and demand conditions. All evaluation methods modify specific unit costs in view of factors affecting property valuation. In Hungary the extreme values of corrections are regularized by an enactment. Inside these values the expert can freely determine every single correction. The spatial databased evaluation (SDBE) method would be able to amend the subjective aspect. The method could primarily be used in local and micro regional cases such as land exchange. The present paper analysis the connection of corrective factors and it introduces the applicability of the SDBE method on a sample area.

articleTitle: Software support of nonparametric control charts
abstract: The topic of this article is software support of nonparametric control charts. The first part of the article focuses on the current situation in SW supporting statistical process control. There are compared the most commonly used SW programs, such as Statgraphics, Minitab, Palstat, and others on the basis of a range of control charts covered by these SW programs, including the nonparametric ones. The second part of the article deals with the presentation of already created SW support for selected nonparametric control charts (Nonparametric Cusum Control Chart, Progressive Mean Control Chart, etc.) within MS Excel. All the obtained knowledge is summarized at the end of this article.

articleTitle: Advanced variable pitch propulsion drive controller
abstract: This article describes behavior of variable pitch propulsion drive controller (VPPDC). This algorithm is applicable for multicopters with variable pitch drives installed. The VPPDC is an extension of standard propulsion drive witch improves its efficiency and extend the flight time. Algorithm is based on knowledge of accurate propeller and brush-less motor properties. Its structure is described in Simulink.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of automated phototherapy system
abstract: Nowadays more and more people are suffering from autoimmune skin diseases. Clinical studies have shown that the 311 Nm narrow-band UVB light's immune-modulating effect decreases symptoms, which can be a good alternative compared to steroid treatments. The purpose of my work is the design and implementation of an automated phototherapy system. The system is a 2 DOF (Degree of freedom) stand, which has the possibility to cover the entire area of the treatment bed. Movement along 2 axes is accomplished with the help of two stepper motors and two motor drivers. The control unit of the system is a Zybo Zynq -7000 SoC development board, running a Linux-based operating system. This system hosts the image processing algorithm, which is responsible for detecting the areas on the patient's skin requiring special treatment. Having identified the target area's location a path planning algorithm calculates the needed step counts, which are afterwards transmitted to the reprogrammable modules in the Zybo FPGA development board. These modules are finite state machines that generate the impulses needed to drive the stepper motor drivers.

articleTitle: Design, modeling and manufacturing analysis of a new rotary combustion engine
abstract: The paper introduces the steps of development of a patented rotary internal combustion engine. First reviews the advantageous features of the novel construction. Then it presents the model structure, the CAD modeling of the prototype and the working simulation using Surface Constructor kinematic modeling and simulation software application. The third part of the paper deals with the modeling and analysis of manufacturing of the most complicated elements, the rotor and the rotary chamber. In the simulation of the grinding procedure of the rotor a patented grinding machine and grinding technology are taken into consideration. The closing part synthesizes the results of the full modeling and simulation process.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of rotary-heart furnace
abstract: Rotary-heart furnace serves for heating steel semi products before tube rolling. This furnace belongs between industry furnaces with a bigger consumption of fuel. Also, the building and reconstruction furnace is expensive. One way as apply unbiased judgement effectiveness of investment design furnace appears mathematical modelling. Therefore, in this paper is briefly described the mathematical dynamical model of rotary-heart furnace and simulation cases. The parametric study results indicated that partial an exchange of the current a cylindrical barrel by a hanging roof a little deteriorates effectiveness and un-uniformity of heated steel charge.

articleTitle: Quality evaluation of heating process control using Matlab tools
abstract: The processing, visualization and analysis of measured data is a basic prerequisite for optimizing processes and designing new, more effective solutions. Current information technologies and advanced sensors allow automatic data collection that can be stored and made available through the web interface. In this paper, the data obtained from the monitoring of the heating process in the selected environment is analysed. The aim is to visualize the monitored data, provide basic statistical information and evaluate the quality of the heating process control using an integral criterion. By using the basic and programmatic tools of the Matlab environment, the user interface will be designed to display the required values based on the user's choice. Thus, the user will be able to compare and analyse data not only within the environment itself but also within time slots.

articleTitle: Smart control of the integrated hydraulic actuator
abstract: The paper presents new concept of control of the linear hydraulic actuator. Linear hydraulic actuators are used in the industry mainly for manipulation with heavy products and in the technologies which requires high forces, dynamic movements and high accuracy. Due to the design of the production equipment's the differential cylinders are used for the realization of the linear hydraulic servo drives controlled by the servovalves. The real properties of the classical concept of the hydraulic servo drive will be summarized and new concept of control based on the full hydraulic resistance bridge will be presented in the paper. Finally, the realization of the integrated actuator will be shown and results from the laboratory testing of the digital closed loop control using the embedded control system will be demonstrated.

articleTitle: A mobile system for data acquisition in traffic management
abstract: This paper we propose a solution to realize of a mobile system for traffic management by counting the number of vehicles on a road with one or two lanes. The traffic intensity is measured using the transducers based on sonar principle. The acquired data are local stored into a local data logger and simultaneous are transmitted via radio communication to a dedicated server. The novelty of this system is represented by the communication facility provided by the new LoRa technology. Also, it is highlights that this system is mobile and it is not invasive on the road structure.

articleTitle: Development of speech-based interface for smart home systems
abstract: In 2019, a team of students and teachers from University of Miskolc is taking part in the Solar Dechatlon Europe Contest. The basic idea of our Project, HoME - HoME from the past for our future-, is to recondition the typical, standardized type of housing in Hungary, the so called Hungarian cube. In the article the plan for the Smart House System of project HoME is going to be presented. The most comfortable way of human communication is speech, which is a possible channel for human-machine interface as well, therefore we are developing a Speech-Based Interface for this Smart System. The interface will not only process verbal commands but also will provide two-way communication.

articleTitle: Intelligent control systems
abstract: Current knowledge of artificial neural networks, fuzzy logic systems, their mathematical foundation and use has been reviewed. Implementation of neural control of anthropomorphic manipulator has been studied, developed and verified in simulation. The results of tests are presented.

articleTitle: Can parallelization save the (computing) world?
abstract: As all other computing laws [1], the computing performance shows a “logistic curve”-like behavior, rather than unlimited growth. Since cca. 2000, the single-processor performance increased only marginally [2], unlike the need for more computing power in the everyday tasks. The stalling forced computer experts to look for alternative methods. The preferred way seems to be to continue the traditions of the single-processor approach: to assemble systems comprising several segregated processors, connected in various ways.

articleTitle: Organisational life assistant: How an IT system can help for the ageing society
abstract: Thanks to the high standard of living and especially the advanced health care system of the developed countries the life expectancy is continuously increasing. Since the human mobility increased as well, the family members often live far from their ageing parents or relatives shifting the responsibility of the elderly care from the individuals to the society. This extra burden on the social care system can be lowered by introducing IT systems, especially designed for elderly users in order to make their self-supporting period longer. The system can help in telemonitoring the living, health and mental condition of the elderly people, the keeping the connection with the relatives from far distance, providing valuable information for doctors and care providers about efficiency or the necessity of a treatment. All together the system gives greater freedom, self-confidence and safer life for the members of the ageing society, provides reassuring information for the relatives about their well-being and reduces the workload of the formal caregivers. Our system predicts advantageous or disadvantageous change in health status in a new approach based on significant change in postural stability. This paper introduces the design consideration, implementation details and usage experience, results of an elderly supporting IT system called Organizational Life Assistant.

articleTitle: Implementation of new adaptive control algorithms in the defined urban area
abstract: This article describes the results of using new approaches in the implementation of intelligent road traffic control algorithms applied in smaller city areas. As a solution of designed traffic-dependent model was the application of different data from the sensor network, which have and can impact on increasing throughput of fully loaded roads in the city but also makes traffic behavior more accurate in the defined area with wider overhead for controlling. The systems outputs optimize traffic parameters of the defined node as well as interconnected intersections with traffic lights and other subsystems according to the traffic situation in the wider area. The article describes not only methodology but also general recommendations that are the result of experience in testing and deploying of adaptive traffic control algorithm in real conditions.

articleTitle: Innovative SQL options in ERP development
abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning Systems provide various core business functions in Financials, Human Resources and Logistics. Oracle and SAP, popular and successful ERP vendors worldwide, continuously improve their products. Standard Query Languages play important roles either during standard or customer developments. Because the execution of Oracle e-Business Suite and SAP Business Suite applications are still based on their relational databases, queries and reports are mainly based on SQL codes designed according to old style, but reliable and robust approaches. It is reasonable to explore how new database technologies and SQL options make changes in design methodologies consequently. This paper discusses some new features of innovative SQL development in SAP, reflecting the effectiveness of innovative options in development. It is found out that developments should designed in a proper way, when old style and new methodologies are balanced for the business functions and also for the company where the developments are introduced.

articleTitle: Decentralized transactive energy management system for distribution systems with prosumer microgrids
abstract: This paper proposes energy scheduling mechanism that establishes competitive market among multiple prosumer microgrids. Prosumers based on the their role will be able to acquire production points (PP) for being a seller or consumption points (CP) for buying energy in the market. Contributions of each individual microgrid are recorded by noval contribution metric (CM) concept. Transactive energy is scheduled in such way that prosumers with higher CM will benefit more, thereby encouraging network users to contribute more and consume less energy. Truthful bidding principle of Vickrey auction is applied to prevent overbidding and underbidding to maintain market in fair state. Blockchain was used to enhance trust between prosumers and shift the market to decentralized state. Strategies to integrate Locational Marginal Pricings (LMPs) into the system were proposed in the paper. The system was simulated using 5 microgrids in IEEE37-bus feeder. Results showed effectiveness of CM based mechanism to manage energy scheduling.

articleTitle: Agriculture autonomous monitoring and decisional mechatronic system
abstract: The article aims to present a complex mechatronic system for Agriculture 4.0 - Automatic Autonomous Monitoring and Decision System for Agriculture (SAAMDA) for potato or vineyard crops. If the implementation of monitoring systems using aerial drones equipped with specialized near-infrared (NIR) inspection systems are already part of the specific themes of the current technological revolution, the solution proposed by the authors is to develop an automated decision and monitoring system, relatively inexpensive, through using customized systems (particular Unmanned Aerial Vehicle <;UAV> structure with modified GoPro Hero 3 Black digital video camera). The proposed system, first of all, unlike existing systems, provides recommendations and decision-making elements for farmers based on crop monitoring, and is also available as a cost accessible to as many users as possible. The price-versus-resolution compromise is compensated by the decision-making algorithm that allows the identification of optimum moments to specific phytosanitary treatments and the harvesting period. At the end of the article, the results of the monitoring and decision system are presented into comparative manner, using the simplified architecture proposed by the authors, versus the results of the advanced monitoring systems, with a series of conclusions.

articleTitle: Efficient implementation of convolutional neural networks on FPGA
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) apply complex machine learning algorithms to process incoming sensor signals to interact with the embedding environment through actuators, which is an inherently real-time task. Therefore, machine learning algorithms must be also evaluated real-time, bringing up very delicate requirements about implementations. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are artificial neural networks successfully applied in machine vision applications, therefore, their use in CPS is primarily determined by the efficiency of the implementation. CNNs are typically implemented using general purpose CPUs, DSPs, and GPGPUs, however, due to their structure and operation, they are also very good candidates to FPGA implementations. The paper will present an efficient implementation of CNNs on FPGAs and an initial evaluation of the implementation using the LeNet network.

articleTitle: Motor controller designed for robotics based on microcontroller with integrated EtherCAT
abstract: The paper focuses on our servo motor controller (SMC) design optimized for robotic applications. This controller is designed to be embedded inside robotic arms or joints to eliminate extensive cabling needed with external centralized controllers. It is based on a single Infineon XMC4800 microcontroller with integrated EtherCAT Slave Controller (ESC), powerful ARM Cortex-M4 CPU core and many peripherals suitable for motor control. This integrated solution provides precise control over distributed system timing. The hardware design contains two-axis three-phase inverter power stage with sigma-delta ADCs for high quality phase current measurement, interfaces for quadrature encoders or hall sensors and encoders with high-speed serial communication protocols and control part with a single microcontroller. The paper provides description of hardware design, software architecture spanning from low level parts to velocity and position control loops with code generated from user reconfigurable function block diagrams and real-time performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Using a graph database for evaluating and enhancing a social reputation engine
abstract: Reputation engines often come with significant computational complexity which limits their realistic applicability in live scenarios. Consequently, there is a usual trade-off between how robust a system is and how fast it can perform. In an attempt to demonstrate the efficiency of our previous proposition called MovieRate, we leveraged the proven ability of graph databases to naturally model vast and dense data while seamlessly traversing through its comprising entities. By detailing how user behaviour in a reviewing platform can be formalised based on both frequency of contributions and personality traits, a module that generates synthetic data for nine types of users was constructed. Similarly, after reviewing various possible types of threats which can generally be expected for a reputation system, a combination of four attacks implying specific user behaviour is outlined. Our experiments showed that even in cases where impressive datasets comprised of millions of entities were used, the system obtains promising execution times. When being faced with attacks, it was additionally validated that malicious users are largely prevented from gaining superior reputation ranks. New directions to improve the system are also given, considering the significant gain in traction for research in the area of integrating social networks, reputation and recommender systems.

articleTitle: Topology-based classification error calculation for symbolic indoor positioning
abstract: The topology-based classification error calculation for symbolic indoor positioning is presented in this paper. Symbolic indoor positioning can be considered as a classification problem, where each category is a symbolic position. The evaluation of classifiers usually follows the CRISP approach, which treats each misclassification equally wrong. However, previous experimental results revealed the demand to distinguish the misclassification errors based on the topology of the building. There are three criteria against the topology-based classification error calculation. Firstly, the method has to take into count the size of the Zones. Secondly, the layout of the Zones has to be considered. Finally, the error values should be proportional to the size of the Zone so the function should be asymmetric. The new approach is based on the gravitational force used in physics, which can be treated as the similarity of two objects, Thus, the gravitational force is inversely proportional with the distance of the Zones and proportional with the product of its capacities. Dissimilarity can be expressed as the reciprocal of the gravitational force. The classification error has to be defined to increase with the dissimilarity of the Zones. Hence the selection of capacity function, and distance function with its reference points has a high impact on the error values. In this paper the method to determine the classification error matrix based on the topology of building is presented.

articleTitle: Improved reference clock connection interface for prototype IEEE 1588 master clocks
abstract: In this paper we present a fundamentally redesigned Global Navigational Satellite System (GNSS) receiver to master clock interface based on our previous design for IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP) master clocks. The new design is optimized for modern timing GNSS receivers; including GPS, Galileo, and GLONASS GNSS; which provide better timing accuracy and precision than previous generic navigational or even older timing GPS receivers. The new design is required because new timing GNSS receivers have lower than 10 ns error while the errors introduced by the previous interface solution is one or two magnitudes bigger than that, causing degraded system wide timing performance for new systems. Better performance is achieved by an error source analysis and a delicate component selection based on the results of the analysis, and in addition, timing oriented PCB routing. Furthermore, the new design is more compact, integrated with a CPU board, and therefore, ready to be deployed in prototype applications. The paper also provides an initial performance evaluation of the improved reference clock interface.

articleTitle: Efficiency analysis of ontology servers
abstract: One of the main current trends in the ICT sector is the widespread use of intelligent devices. We can witness the expansion of the IoT architecture where smart devices can interact with each other and they can operate as intelligent agents to control our environment. Usually, these devices have a local knowledge base providing information for the concrete actions. In order to implement a higher level of intelligence, the devices should interact with humans in a more general environment. The main representation form of common sense knowledge in intelligent applications is ontology. Consequently, a widescope and detailed knowledge base that can cover general requirements should be stored in a general ontology server. This means that ontology databases should be able to manage huge amount of data in an efficient way. Although the concept of computerized ontology management is almost 10 years old (Gruber introduced this term in 2009), currently we have experiences only with smaller and separate ontologies. We can expect though that the future development trends in IoT will require the implementation of new kinds of large scale ontology servers, too. This paper presents first the main requirements on a general ontology server focusing on the demands in an IoT architecture. The main goal of the paper is then to compare the efficiency of three implementation alternatives: native RDF triplet storage, relational database storage and graph database storage.

articleTitle: Graph-based database architecture and data preprocessing for analysis of 2D dynamic systems
abstract: This article proposes the computational approach for the analysis of dynamic systems. Traditionally such systems are presented in transfer function or state matrices forms, the second one being especially convenient for computation with tools such as MATLAB environment. The problem with such approach arises when very large number of forms of dynamic system need to be compared and analysed, as finding similarities and properties is time-consuming or outright impossible due to computational complexity problems. Due to such limitations it is impossible to analyse all possible solutions for given dynamic systems and determine their usability. As solution to such problem alternative approach is proposed, where all possible representations of dynamic system are created using fast GPGPU (General-Purpose computing on Graphics Processor Units) compatible algorithm and stored in the form of directed graphs (digraphs). Creating efficient database architecture for storage of large number (numbering in millions) of such graphs in graph-based database like Neo4j allows us to efficiently analyse a whole set of solutions to find similarities, hidden properties and limitations, while at the same time retaining the ability to store the obtained data for further analysis (especially of more complicated systems) and expand the solution size, efficiently building new solutions on base of simpler solutions stored in the database.

articleTitle: Modelling the tongue movement of Chinese Shaanxi Xi'an dialect speech
abstract: Visual speech play a significant role in speech perception especially for deaf and hard of hearing people or normal people in noisy environment. Lip reading depends on visible articulators to improve speech perception. However, not only the movement of lip and face provide part of phonetic information, but also the motion of the tongue which is generally not entirely seen carries an important part of the articulatory information not accessible through lip reading. First, static viseme (visual representation of a phoneme) classification of Chinese Shaanxi Xi'an dialect speech was performed according to the method that carried out to classify Mandarin (Standard Chinese) static viseme. Then we carried out an experiment with the purpose to study both the timing and position properties of articulatory movements of the tongue in VCV and CVC utterances of Chinese Shaanxi Xi'an dialect speech in different tempo. The speech materials conclude VCV and CVC sequences were recorded via `Micro' ultrasound system that eventually form the JPG images and MP4 videos with the help of Assistant Advanced software. We have developed an algorithm that can automatically carry out a spatial-temporal tracking of tongue movement contour from the ultrasound images we recorded of one speaker who read randomized lists of VCV utterances containing the vowels /e, a/ and CVC utterances containing the consonants /k, t/ in all possible combinations covering all phoneme - 26 consonants and 41 vowels of Shaanxi Xi'an dialect. The extracted visual information gained by this method is then classified in order to define the uttered viseme and is used to create dynamic viseme system of tongue for Shaanxi Xi'an dialect. This dynamic viseme system is used to create the fundamentals of a talking head - animated articulation model for Shaanxi Xi'an dialect speech. The talking head is going to be utilized in a speech assistant system assisting the speech improvement of hard of hearing children and training for second language learners.

articleTitle: Simulation of acacia gasification process with variable operating pressure and temperature
abstract: This electronic document presents the thermokinetical modelling of the gasification process done on acacia-tree with variable operating conditions and different humidity levels. Gasification does not produce flue gas, but due to imperfect burning, synthesis gas appears which is rich in flammable components (CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>). The chemical structure of this gas depends on the components of the fuel and the humidity level, but greatly affected by the technological parameters too, such as pressure and temperature, as well as the air-ratio. The study shows the change in the amount of the fuel and the reaction efficiency, caused by varying gasification temperature and pressure. Rising temperature results in improved efficiency, while higher pressure worsens reaction efficiency. However, at higher temperature intervals, the effect of the pressure is neglectable.
